message.text: You are right: that is a design mistake. Cards are already plain files (a folder and a page.jsonl each), and every folder's page.jsonl already lists its children. So AI 2 can READ everything as static files, in production too. Servex should only be needed to WRITE (dev only) and for live agent status, which quietly disappears without it. task-mastermind-ai2-static (Sonnet) is making that change.

AI 2 now reads its cards from plain files: a small index, ai/cards.jsonl (one line per card), plus each card's own page.jsonl. I chose the index over walking all ~400 folders because a walk is a request storm; the browser falls back to walking the day pages if the index is missing. Servex only keeps the index fresh on each write, and is used for writes, live agents and the push. Proof on the live site: with ?servex=http://127.0.0.1:59999 (nothing there) all 329 cards show, including today's 09/25 ones, with no script errors. The only console line is Chrome's own "connection refused" for the single probe, and a production host makes no Servex request at all. The New card button hides when Servex is down. The normal load also shows 0 errors. Two things to know: the new index is only kept fresh after the next Servex restart (until then cards.jsonl is a snapshot I generated); and the changes are uncommitted in the main tree (the branch worktree/ai2-static has the commit), because the tree already holds other agents' edits in the same files. I could not reach task-mastermind-layout-check to coordinate, but I did not touch sorting or filtering. Files: /framework/ai2/inbox.js, /framework/ai2/fold.js, Servex/cards/Cards.js.
